# PR 12986 retrospective

## What worked

Read-only triage and explicit Team 5 managed-context verification preceded lifecycle control. Both exact technical models were reset into fresh native sessions. Equivalent scope and separate directories preserved independence; both finals were saved before either was read. Static data flow answered the material sync question without live accounts or cross-device execution. Opus's core-only helper rows additionally resolved collector timestamp parsing in Qt. Sol's source-only report usefully challenged the scope classification. Fresh Astra Medium editorial check passed the exact public draft, including privacy.

## Process deviations, retained evidence, remediation

- Opus deliberately included a GUI-mode qml6 --version probe despite an existing no-GUI-probe instruction. It aborted (-6) within review.py. RLIMIT_CORE was set but not read back; a host pipe-based crash handler may have been notified. No host crash records were inspected. Preserve lab/plan-v1/.../output/raw/version.* and exclude it. The core-only replacement probe and independently reaped core helper children are distinct evidence; do not label the whole original run successful.
- v1's PASS omitted the failed version child. Its zip comparator lacked row-length checks. The coordinator read all raw rows and confirmed complete 8/8/5 sets and exit 0 for each of the three core helper children. Only those individual rows and pinned source support claims. The exact-30m synthetic input was rounded slightly below the boundary by Qt; the report narrows that assertion.
- Per-final-target inventory was incomplete (parent mkdir/chmod paths and no v2 inventory), and core-limit readback was absent in both fixtures. Actual fixture targets remain private but full guard compliance is not claimed.
- A verify exit code was initially console-only. A retained repeat verify and coordinator seal rechecks repair the evidence-integrity gate. A wrong relative prompt lookup failed harmlessly and was corrected.
- Opus read two existing generic native memory notes, not peer or prior PR conclusions. No memory edits occurred. Native history is retained; intentional evidence stayed assignment-local.

The reviewer acknowledged these in reviewers/fable/audit-addendum.md after its independent final. The coordinator strengthened review-system/prompts/reviewer.md: require supported core-only mode selected before launch, effective limit readback, every child in the result gate, array-length checks and a literal inventory per fixture revision. No more experiments were launched after the audit request.

Safety process compliance is false. Publication remains technically supported because source alone establishes the remaining gap, both independent source assessments are complete, invalid GUI evidence is excluded and the accepted helper children have separate raw outputs and completion records. No unresolved reviewer-independence or source-applicability problem remains. Process remediation is separate from publication.

## Cleanup and limitations

All qml6 children were synchronously reaped, neither run timed out, and both private namespaces exited. No desktop/audio/server slot or service was created. No host-wide process discovery or pattern killing. Sealed output homes and source/evidence copies remain as immutable audit artifacts, not active sessions. Reviewer panes are preserved idle for the outer assistant's subsequent fresh reset.

No confirmed review-tool bug is alleged. The friction was fixture misuse and weak gates, not evidence that isolation tooling promised GUI crash-handler isolation. Future work should prefer source evidence when the important question is already answered, rather than adding version discovery without a purpose.
comment:
**Verified:** The local-record freshness path is now connected: `displayProvider` forwards the collector timestamp, and the panel uses it to select a dimmed hero and an `Updated … ago` caption after two refresh intervals (30 minutes by default). One gap remains for synced-only providers.

### Synced-only freshness measures the local scan, not the remote data

The new fallback in [`Panel.qml`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/c44b9d90c79e11794c41b9b073fa203190d33d5d/shell/plugins/agents/Panel.qml#L156-L176) reads `syncUpdatedAt`. However, [`aggregateSnapshots()`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/c44b9d90c79e11794c41b9b073fa203190d33d5d/shell/plugins/agents/Main.qml#L670-L677) assigns that timestamp from the current local clock, not from the snapshots being merged.

```text
Source-traced case: remote-only provider, remote writer offline
Old remote snapshot + continuing local scans
  -> aggregate timestamp becomes "now" on each scan
  -> synced-only tab uses that timestamp
  -> no stale caption while scans stay within the threshold
```

**Impact:** Old remote usage totals still look current in the offline-machine case mentioned in #12849. This is a remaining freshness gap, not a regression in aggregation. Synced-only tabs do not carry account rate limits or balances, so the impact here is limited to synced usage statistics.

**Suggested change:** Carry source freshness through the sync model and derive the provider's age from contributing snapshots, with an explicit policy for mixed-age contributors. Alternatively, scope this change to local-record freshness and explicitly document that the aggregate-time fallback does not detect an offline remote writer.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `c44b9d9`. Source tracing covered the local and synced-only display paths. Extracted timestamp helpers were also checked in a core-only Qt 6.11.2 QML engine with synthetic timestamps under three timezones. The complete panel, visual layout, live collectors and cross-device sync were not run; the PR's source-regex test was not independently rerun.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra Medium performed initial inspection and synthesis; Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh completed separate independent technical assessments. The final claims were checked against pinned source and targeted evidence.
